title: Practice Exam 9
description: An additional full-length 36-question simulated California Class C knowledge exam.

questions.question: What should a pedestrian do when the 'DON'T WALK' or upraised-hand symbol begins flashing while they are still in the crosswalk?
choices: Finish crossing to the other side; do not start a new crossing
Stop immediately and return to the curb they came from
Stay in the middle of the road until the next WALK signal
Begin crossing only if no cars are visible
questions.explanation: A flashing 'DON'T WALK'/hand means do not begin crossing, but anyone already in the crosswalk should continue safely to the far side.

questions.question: Why should you be especially careful driving near schools at the start and end of the school day?
choices: Children may be distracted and dart into the street unexpectedly
Speed limits are higher at those times
Crossing guards leave at those times
Traffic signals turn off
questions.explanation: Children can be unpredictable and distracted near schools, often stepping into the road without looking, so drive slowly and stay alert.

questions.question: At an intersection, you are stopped at a red light and want to turn right. A pedestrian is crossing the street you want to enter. What must you do?
choices: Wait for the pedestrian to finish crossing before turning
Turn quickly behind the pedestrian as long as you do not touch them
Honk to let the pedestrian know you are turning
Proceed because pedestrians must yield to turning vehicles
questions.explanation: Even on a legal right turn at a red light, you must yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk and may turn only when it is safe.

questions.question: How does alcohol affect your vision, especially at night?
choices: It reduces night vision and the ability to judge distances
It improves your ability to see in the dark
It widens your field of vision
It has no effect on vision
questions.explanation: Alcohol impairs night vision, depth perception, and the ability to judge distances and speeds, making nighttime driving especially dangerous.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Alcohol, Drugs, and Driving

questions.question: What is the single most important thing to do before changing lanes?
choices: Make sure the lane you want to move into is clear and safe
Increase your speed by at least 10 mph
Turn on your hazard lights
Tap your brakes to warn the car behind you
questions.explanation: The most important step before changing lanes is ensuring the destination lane is clear by checking mirrors and your blind spot.

questions.question: While driving on the freeway, where should you keep your eyes to drive safely?
choices: Keep your eyes moving, scanning the road far ahead and checking mirrors
Fixed on the vehicle directly in front of you
Focused only on the lane line beside you
Mostly on the dashboard instruments
questions.explanation: At freeway speeds you should keep your eyes moving, scanning well ahead and regularly checking mirrors and to the sides so you can spot hazards early.

questions.question: In California, drivers under the age of 18 may use a cell phone while driving:
choices: Not at all — even hands-free use is prohibited
Only if it is hands-free
Only for texting at red lights
Whenever a passenger is present
questions.explanation: Drivers under 18 are banned from using any cell phone while driving, including hands-free devices. The only exception is a true emergency.

questions.question: What is the best way to combat "highway hypnosis" or drowsiness on a long freeway drive?
choices: Stop to rest, get fresh air, or switch drivers, and keep your eyes moving
Turn the heater up and stare straight ahead
Drive faster to reach your destination sooner
Use cruise control and close your eyes briefly
questions.explanation: To avoid highway hypnosis and fatigue, take breaks, get fresh air, keep your eyes scanning the road, and pull over to rest if you feel drowsy.

questions.question: What is the maximum speed for a vehicle towing a trailer, or for a vehicle with three or more axles, on the highway?
choices: 55 mph
65 mph
60 mph
45 mph
questions.explanation: Vehicles towing trailers and any vehicle with three or more axles are limited to 55 mph, even where higher limits are posted.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Maximum Speed Limit

questions.question: When a bicyclist is riding in the bike lane ahead and you plan to turn right, you should:
choices: Signal, then merge into the bike lane before turning while checking for cyclists
Make the right turn from the regular lane across the bike lane
Turn quickly before the cyclist arrives
Stop in the travel lane and turn from there
questions.explanation: When permitted, merge into the bike lane within 200 feet of the corner, checking for cyclists, before completing your right turn.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Sharing the Road with Bicyclists

questions.question: Reading or looking at a navigation screen for several seconds while driving is an example of a:
choices: Visual distraction
Mechanical distraction
Auditory benefit
Manual-only distraction
questions.explanation: Looking away from the road at a screen is a visual distraction because your eyes leave the driving scene.

questions.question: When the road is wet, how should you adjust your speed to keep control?
choices: Reduce your speed below the posted limit because stopping distance increases on wet pavement
Maintain the posted speed since tires grip the same when wet
Increase speed to push water away from the tires
Drive at the speed of surrounding traffic no matter what
questions.explanation: Wet roads lengthen stopping distance and reduce traction, so the Basic Speed Law requires you to slow below the posted limit for safe control.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — California's Basic Speed Law

questions.question: When parking a manual-transmission vehicle on a hill, which gear should you leave it in?
choices: First gear when facing uphill, reverse when facing downhill
Neutral regardless of direction
Reverse when facing uphill, first gear when facing downhill
Whatever gear it was in when you stopped
questions.explanation: For a manual transmission, leave it in first (low) gear when facing uphill and in reverse when facing downhill, along with the parking brake.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Parking on a Hill

questions.question: A five-sided (pentagon) sign warns you that you are approaching:
choices: A school zone or school crossing
A railroad crossing
A hospital
A construction zone
questions.explanation: The pentagon-shaped sign indicates a school zone or school crossing ahead; watch for children.

questions.question: You are about to enter a road from a private driveway and a vehicle is approaching on the road. Who has the right of way?
choices: The vehicle already traveling on the road
You, because you signaled first
Whoever is going faster
You, if your vehicle is larger
questions.explanation: When entering a roadway from a driveway, you must yield to all traffic already on the main road.

questions.question: You are parking on a hill that has a curb. The car is facing uphill. Which way should you turn the front wheels?
choices: Away from the curb, so the car rolls back into the curb
Toward the curb, so the car rolls into traffic
Straight ahead, parallel to the curb
It does not matter which way the wheels point
questions.explanation: When facing uphill with a curb, turn the wheels away from the curb and let the car roll back a little so a tire rests against the curb.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Parking on a Hill

questions.question: In California, holding and using a hand-held cell phone while driving is:
choices: Illegal for all drivers
Legal as long as you are over 21
Legal only on city streets
Legal if the call lasts under one minute
questions.explanation: It is illegal to hold and use a hand-held phone while driving. Adults 18 and over may only use a phone in hands-free mode.

questions.question: What does a solid white line between two lanes traveling the same direction mean?
choices: Lane changes are discouraged; stay in your lane
Lane changes are encouraged across it
It marks the edge of the roadway
You may stop and park along it
questions.explanation: A solid white line discourages lane changes; you should generally stay in your lane rather than cross it.

questions.question: If a person authorized to direct traffic signals you to stop while the traffic signal shows green, which instruction controls?
choices: The traffic officer's instruction takes priority over the signal
The green light takes priority over the officer
Whichever you noticed first
You may choose either since both are valid
questions.explanation: Directions given by a peace officer or other authorized person directing traffic must be obeyed even when they conflict with a signal or sign.

questions.question: What is the maximum speed limit in an alley?
choices: 15 mph
25 mph
10 mph
20 mph
questions.explanation: The speed limit in any alley is 15 mph.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Maximum Speed Limit

questions.question: You should be especially alert for pedestrians:
choices: Near bus stops, crosswalks, schools, and in residential areas
Only on freeways
Only at night
Only in rural areas
questions.explanation: Pedestrians are common near bus stops, crosswalks, schools, and residential areas, so stay especially alert in these places.

questions.question: A yellow advisory speed sign mounted below a curve warning sign tells you what?
choices: The recommended safe speed for the curve under good conditions
The legal maximum speed enforced by police
The minimum speed you must maintain in the curve
The distance to the curve in feet
questions.explanation: A yellow advisory speed plaque suggests a safe speed for the curve in good conditions; you should go even slower in rain, fog, or at night.

questions.question: After a first DUI conviction, a driver can expect:
choices: Fines, license suspension, possible jail, and a required DUI program
A warning letter with no other consequences
Only a small fine and no license action
Loss of vehicle registration but no license penalty
questions.explanation: A first DUI brings fines, license suspension, possible jail time, and completion of a court-ordered DUI program.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Alcohol, Drugs, and Driving

questions.question: In which situation should you increase your following distance to four or more seconds?
choices: When the road is wet, foggy, or you are following a motorcycle
When traffic is light and the road is dry
When you are driving on a one-way street
When you are first in line at a red light
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance to four or more seconds in rain, fog, at night, when towing, or when following motorcycles or large vehicles.

questions.question: If a ball rolls into the street near a school or park, you should:
choices: Slow down and be ready to stop, as a child may run after it
Continue at your speed since the ball is harmless
Speed up to get past quickly
Honk and keep driving
questions.explanation: A ball in the road often means a child may chase after it; slow down and be prepared to stop.

questions.question: You are approaching an intersection when a funeral procession begins to pass through against your green light. What should you do?
choices: Yield to the entire procession and let it pass before proceeding
Cut into the middle of the procession since you have a green light
Follow closely behind the lead car to merge with the procession
Proceed normally because the procession must obey the signal
questions.explanation: A funeral procession led by a traffic officer has the right-of-way. Yield and do not cut through the procession, even if you have a green light.

questions.question: A white rectangular sign reading 'KEEP RIGHT' with a downward diagonal arrow means what?
choices: Stay to the right of a divider, median, or obstruction ahead
A right turn is required at the next intersection
Slower traffic must exit on the right
The right lane is closed ahead
questions.explanation: This regulatory sign directs drivers to pass to the right of an island, median, or obstruction in the roadway.

questions.question: A yellow painted curb allows you to do what?
choices: Stop only long enough to load or unload passengers or freight, usually for commercial vehicles
Park your car for up to two hours
Stop only to pick up or drop off passengers
Park only with a disabled placard
questions.explanation: A yellow curb means stop no longer than the time posted to load or unload passengers or freight; drivers of noncommercial vehicles usually must stay with the vehicle.

questions.question: Why should you leave extra following distance behind a large truck or bus?
choices: Large vehicles block your view ahead, so more room helps you see and react
Large vehicles can stop much faster than cars
It is illegal to follow a truck within three seconds
Trucks always travel slower than the speed limit
questions.explanation: Following a large vehicle too closely blocks your view of the road ahead; extra distance lets you see hazards sooner.

questions.question: When a bicyclist makes a left turn from a roadway, they are entitled to:
choices: Use the left lane or turn lane like other vehicles
Only turn from the right curb
Use the crosswalk while riding
Stop all traffic before turning
questions.explanation: Because bicyclists follow the same rules as drivers, they may move into the left turn lane to make a left turn.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Sharing the Road with Bicyclists

questions.question: From a one-way street onto another one-way street, when is a left turn on a red light allowed?
choices: After stopping completely and yielding, unless a sign prohibits it
It is never allowed in any circumstance
Only when a green arrow is shown
Whenever the cross street has no traffic, without stopping
questions.explanation: California allows a left turn on red from a one-way street onto another one-way street after a complete stop and yielding, unless prohibited by a sign.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Traffic Signal Lights

questions.question: A tire suddenly blows out while you are driving on the freeway. What should you do first?
choices: Grip the wheel firmly, ease off the gas, and steer straight
Brake hard immediately to stop as fast as possible
Turn the wheel sharply toward the shoulder
Accelerate to regain control of the vehicle
questions.explanation: If a tire blows out, hold the steering wheel firmly, take your foot off the gas, and let the vehicle slow gradually before easing off the road; do not brake hard.

questions.question: A yellow diamond sign showing a leaping deer means what?
choices: Deer or other animals may cross the road; watch for them
A wildlife refuge prohibits stopping here
Hunting is permitted in this area
A petting zoo or farm exit is ahead
questions.explanation: The deer symbol on a yellow diamond is a warning that animals frequently cross the roadway, so drivers should be alert and ready to slow.

questions.question: After an emergency vehicle has passed you and you have pulled over, when may you return to driving?
choices: After it has passed and you have checked that the way is clear of any other emergency vehicles
Immediately, without checking for other vehicles
Only after waiting a full five minutes
Only after the siren can no longer be heard at all, regardless of traffic
questions.explanation: Wait until the emergency vehicle has passed, then check that no additional emergency vehicles are coming before merging back into traffic.

questions.question: A red 'X' displayed over a lane on a multi-lane road means what?
choices: The lane is closed and you must not drive in it
The lane is reserved for carpools only
You may use the lane only to pass
The lane is open but has a lower speed limit
questions.explanation: A red 'X' lane-control signal means the lane is closed to traffic; move out of it. A green downward arrow over a lane means it is open for use.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Lane Use Control Signals

questions.question: How closely are you allowed to follow a fire engine that is responding to an alarm?
choices: No closer than 300 feet
No closer than 100 feet
No closer than 500 feet
No closer than 50 feet
questions.explanation: You must not follow within 300 feet of any fire engine, police vehicle, ambulance, or other emergency vehicle responding with a siren or flashing lights.
